title: Engineering task contract
description: Validated at creation. A task that cannot state how it will be proven correct is not a task, and this schema rejects it.

title.description: Must name a specific behaviour. 'Build authentication' is too vague to verify; 'Implement applicant invitation creation and one-time token validation' names something testable.

context.description: Paths or doc anchors the agent must read first. This is where project-specific knowledge enters a generic role.

harness_task.description: Explicitly opts a task into maintaining harness CODE. Absence means false: a task that does not declare it is treated exactly as every task is today, with write access under aiteam/** a hard scope violation. The exemption is never inferred from the file list, the title, or anything else; it only opens WHICH paths a task may list in files.expected, never the list itself. It never permits .aiteam/** (harness state, the machinery of judgement) and never permits skipping review — a harness task must pass independent review, enforced by the transition gate rather than trusted to this field.

acceptance_criteria.description: Each criterion names the test that proves it, so 'criteria met' is grep-checkable rather than a matter of opinion.

verified_by.description: test:<file>::<name> for automated proof, or manual:<what the orchestrator must observe> when no test can express it.

mutation.description: How to break the behaviour this criterion asserts, so the harness can prove the criterion's test is capable of failing. A test that still passes once its guard is removed proves nothing, and green tests of that kind have twice reached review in this project. The reviewer runs read-only and cannot execute container-backed tests, so this is the only automated check on test honesty.

file.description: Path, relative to the worktree, holding the guard.

find.description: Exact source text implementing the guard. Must appear exactly once.

replace.description: What to put in its place. Defaults to empty, i.e. delete the guard.

test.description: Test-name filter passed to the runner. With the guard removed this test MUST fail.

expected.description: Globs the task may write. Used both to detect scope violations and to schedule non-colliding tasks in parallel.

lens.description: Overlays layered onto the role prompt. Lenses are how a generic role acquires a specialist's attention without absorbing project vocabulary.

counterexample_runner.description: Per-task override for the command that executes counterexamples. Defaults to the vitest runner when absent; a task whose tests are shell scripts (a finding against aiteam/**) names its own runner here. Read by bin/counterexample.sh.

mutation_runner.description: Per-task override for the command that executes mutation checks. Defaults to the vitest runner when absent. Read by bin/mutate.sh.

verification.description: Shell commands run in the worktree. Their recorded exit code, not the agent's report, decides whether the task advances.

findings.description: Carried verbatim from review into the remediation task. Summarising findings loses the detail that made them actionable.

waiver.$comment: The owner's recorded decision to accept work over a failing review. It never alters the verdict, the findings or the unmet criteria — those stay exactly as the reviewer wrote them. Every field is required because a waiver without a decider, a reason or a successor task is indistinguishable from the finding being forgotten.

waived_to.$comment: The task that now carries the findings. Gates refuse a waiver naming a task that is DONE, ABANDONED or absent.
